thread:
Aisha (AE): Hey team, Tallship wants to run a short POC next week. They want two model variants: `tship-llama-7b-finetuned` (vanilla) and a custom quantized variant they built `tship-7b-q4_custom`. Can we confirm catalog fit + any ops/security blockers? They care about 100qps peak, 256 token avg, and sub-150ms p95 on dedicated GPUs.
Sam M (Eng): Do we have that tship model/variant in the catalog currently? If not, will it require special kernel work / vetting?
Chen Li (Solutions): Not in verified catalog yet. From the model spec they sent, attention/adapter layers are non-standard — could break our KV-cache optimizations. Need to run an offline compatibility check.
Maria G (Sales-Eng): Also flagging security asks: customer requires KMS integration for keys (BYOK), SOC2 audit summary, and an IP/data flow diagram. They asked whether Private (VPC) deploy is needed or if Dedicated suffices.
ops-bot: Note: Reserved capacity required for 100qps sustained. Estimated commit: 2 x A100-80GB or equivalent.
Sam M (Eng): Chen — can you try the quick inspect? use `redwoodctl model inspect --model tship-llama-7b-finetuned --variant q4_0` against the sample artifact they provided. If KV-cache flags, we need a compatibility shim or disable prefix caching for that variant.
Chen Li (Solutions): Ran the inspect locally, output: `ATTN_LAYERS: custom_adapter; KV_CACHE: incompatible (adapter modifies key/query dims)` — quick dump: ```{
  model: tship-llama-7b-finetuned
  variant: q4_0
  kv_cache: incompatible
  recommended_action: disable_kv_cache or map_adapter
}``` Not pretty but actionable.
Aisha (AE): If KV cache is incompatible, what does that mean for latency/cost? Will they hit 150ms p95?
Sam M (Eng): Without KV cache we lose prefix reuse — latency will rise and token cost per request up. For 256 tokens and 100qps, rough est: 1.8x GPU time per token. Could still meet 150ms p95 on beefy nodes but cost jumps. I can run a micro-benchmark if they share a sample prompt distribution.
Maria G (Sales-Eng): Pricing question from buyer: can we provide a blended price for the POC (dedicated + support) vs hosted per-token? They want a short 2-week POC.
Aisha (AE): We usually offer a POC rate and provisional reserved pricing. Sam — can you give a ballpark monthly estimate for 2x A100s with no KV cache? Include support/engineer hours (can be a range).
Sam M (Eng): Ballpark: ~$30k-45k/mo infra for the reserved GPUs + 40-80 engineering hours for onboarding/troubleshooting. If we keep KV cache enabled it drops to ~$18k-25k/mo. I'll make a mini quote.
Chen Li (Solutions): Security: BYOK/KMS — our Private and Dedicated both support external KMS via customer-managed keys, but if they want HSM-backed keys in-host, that needs Private deployment. Also need to send our standard SOC2 summary + data-flow doc. Maria — I'll attach a simple network diagram in an email.
Maria G (Sales-Eng): Noted. Buyer asked about model pinning and fallback: can we do automatic fallback to a verified open model if custom variant fails? They want SLA.
Sam M (Eng): Yes — we can configure routing policy: primary -> `tship-7b-q4_custom`, fallback -> `redwood-verif-llama7b-q4`. Fallback increases latency on failure but keeps app online. We'll need to set canary and health checks before routing 100% traffic.
Aisha (AE): Action items: (1) Chen run a compatibility scan on both artifacts + send a short results note (2) Sam produce a POC infra + cost estimate + fallback plan (3) Maria gather security pack (SOC2, data flow, KMS notes) and flag if Private is required. I will coordinate dates with the customer for next-week start.
Chen Li (Solutions): Started the deeper test — running `redwoodctl run-compat-suite --artifact ./tship_artifact.tar.gz --tests kv,quant,kernel` will give a full report (should be done in ~1h). I’ll paste results here.
ops-bot: Reminder: If we enable a custom quantized variant on Dedicated, add a preflight to confirm kernel availability across nodes.
Maria G (Sales-Eng): I'll draft the security email and ask for the buyer's security questionnaire now. Aisha — do we have a standard POC agreement template?
Aisha (AE): Yes — sales-legal POC template lives in /wiki/sales/poc-template. I'll attach it in the follow-up thread.
Sam M (Eng): If Chen's report says `kv_cache: incompatible`, short-term path: disable prefix caching for that model and enable a warm-hot worker pool (smaller batch size, more nodes) to hit latency. Long term: engage inference team to map adapter dims into our kernel (could take 2-3 sprints).
Chen Li (Solutions): Compat suite finished: key outputs: `kv_cache: incompatible`, `quant: supported (q4_0 variant ok)`, `kernel_fallback: required for adapter` — I'll upload the full report to the deal repo and tag you all.
Aisha (AE): Great — thanks. I'll propose a 2-week POC with Dedicated capacity, fallback to verified model, and a POC credit to offset the extra infra cost. Will follow up with dates and attach the report + POC template. :thumbsup:
Maria G (Sales-Eng): Perfect — I'll include the KMS/BYOK note and ask buyer if Private is a hard requirement.
Sam M (Eng): I'll draft the infra/cost note by EOD. If we need to tweak the runtime, give a 2-week runway for eng changes.
Aisha (AE): Closing loop here — next steps captured. Thanks team!
